maria (eng-runtime): Heads-up: ran a perf profile on 8xA100 TP=4 inference with kv-cache and saw a big transient bump in GPU memory right after the first forward. looks like NCCL comm buffers + temporary per-shard allocations are spiking and causing OOMs on some configs. attaching profiler snippet below.

akshay (eng-ml): can you paste the profiler output? is it during prefix warmup or steady-state?

maria (eng-runtime): it's right after warmup when multiple requests hit concurrently. steady-state is fine. profiler sampled with nvprof + our internal tracer:
```
[PROFILE] timeline: forward_start -> alloc_commbuf (120MB) -> nccl_allreduce -> tmp_alloc(256MB) -> forward -> free_tmp -> free_commbuf
[MEM] reserved=40GiB used=34.8GiB peak=36.3GiB
[NOTES] per-tensor-parallel-shard: commbufs allocated per-shard instead of shared, tmp buffers allocated with default allocator (no reuse)
```

tomek (eng-infra): hmm, we've seen similar when `cudaMalloc` fallback happens a bunch. are we on cudaMallocAsync or preallocated arena?

maria (eng-runtime): runner is using our arena allocator but comm bufs are allocated outside arena by NCCL / comm primitives. so they end up in cudaMalloc path if size > workspace slice. also tmp allocations for attention kernels are ~single-use.

jen (eng-runtime): @maria can you share the model size / seq len / batch shape? helps determine shard footprint.

maria (eng-runtime): model ~2.8B, seq len 2048, dynamic batch: bursts of 8 requests x 4 tokens. TP=4 => shard size ~700MB raw params. commbufs observed ~80-130MB each shard depending on kernel.

akshay (eng-ml): possible mitigations: 1) reuse a per-device comm slab allocated at startup and slice it for shards, 2) switch kernels to stream-friendly inplace reductions so temporary buffers shrink, 3) pre-reserve tmp workspace for fastest kernels (like fused attention).

tomek (eng-infra): slab idea looks promising. if we allocate a single NCCL comm buffer pool per GPU and hand out offsets for each tensor-parallel op, we avoid cudaMalloc churn. downside: we need to size it conservatively or implement eviction heuristics.

maria (eng-runtime): sketched a quick patch that allocates `comm_slab_size = min(ceil(total_shard_comm * 1.2), MAX_SLAB)` at startup per-gpu and uses it for all NCCL ops. initial results: eliminated the 120MB transient spikes but introduced fragmentation for some kernel tmp patterns.

jen (eng-runtime): did you also try enabling `cudaMallocAsync` + pooling? that reduces peak but still has per-call meta overhead.

maria (eng-runtime): yes, with `cudaMallocAsync` the tail latencies improved but peak memory didn't drop enough for worst-case bursts. the slab avoids peak growth but we need to address tmp workspace reuse.

akshay (eng-ml): for tmp workspace: we should add a lifetime-based reuse pass in the kernel scheduler. i.e., scan the forward graph, compute max concurrent workspace need, and allocate a shared workspace per-stream. many fp16 kernels have short lifetimes and can share the same buffer.

tomek (eng-infra): agree. also add a fallback throttle: if slab usage + reserved tmp > threshold, route to lower-memory variant (cpu offload or quantized kernel) or queue requests. can integrate with smart routing policies.

maria (eng-runtime): quick repro config I used:
```
RWD_TP=4 RWD_SEQ=2048 RWD_BATCH_BURST=8 RWD_USE_ASYNC_ALLOC=1
prof: nvprof --profile-from-start off --print-gpu-trace
```
Patch diff is small: allocate slab at init, replace `cudaMalloc` in comm path with `slab.alloc(size)`, fallback to arena/cudaMalloc if slab full.

jen (eng-runtime): any perf regressions from using slab alloc? I worry kernel codepaths may expect contiguous allocations per-op.

maria (eng-runtime): latency stable; slight +2% on tiny requests due to extra bookkeeping. throughput unchanged. main risk is fragmentation: if we hand out many small slices, we may leave uncoalesced gaps. planning compaction at safe points (between requests).

akshay (eng-ml): also check NCCL's internal behavior: some collectives internally allocate temp workspace per op (for e.g., alltoall with non-power-of-two sizes). Could be worth switching to NCCL primitives that accept user buffers to avoid internal mallocs.

tomek (eng-infra): good point. can we pass pre-allocated buffers to NCCL ops in our wrapper? that relies on their API but iirc `ncclAllReduce` takes in/out pointers only; internal buffers still used. need to audit versions.

maria (eng-runtime): next steps I'm taking: 1) add slab + compaction test harness, 2) implement kernel-level shared tmp workspace sched pass, 3) run matrix of TP (2,4,8), batch burst sizes, seq len, and NCCL versions. will post numbers.

jen (eng-runtime): sg. if you want I'll help run the nightly fleet jobs across regions. add a boolean flag so we can toggle slab at runtime. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: build/1799002001: perf-test-nccl-slab passed on 8xA100 (regressions: 0, peak-mem -7%), diffs at /ci/artifacts/1799002001

maria (eng-runtime): awesome, thanks @jen and @sre-bot. I'll upload the patch and a short writeup with profiling traces. If we can get slab+tmp-reuse in next week, might close a few OOM support tickets.

akshay (eng-ml): one more ask: let's add a small eval that asserts memory headroom for 95th percentile concurrent bursts. that'll prevent silent regressions.

maria (eng-runtime): good call. will add a watchdog.

jen (eng-runtime): cool. ping me when it's in a draft PR and I'll review the runtime API bits.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks all, filing follow-ups in GH and will attach perf artifacts here. :rocket:
